need: Clarify what a scanner profile owns versus what is configured per Gravity Forms form.
candidates: Profile-level parser/output contract; per-form field mapping.
observed_result: Owner confirmed: Sayad profile declares the number/order/meaning of parsed outputs so the scanner knows how to parse; actual Gravity Forms target fields are chosen when designing each form.
decision: Profile owns parser schema/output keys and validation; each Structured Scanner instance maps those output keys to ordinary Gravity Forms fields in that form. Treat output keys as merge-tag-like symbolic tokens for UI/mental model, not as stored data or literal GF Merge Tags.
reopen_condition: Reopen only if the Form Builder POC shows per-instance output-to-field mapping is unreliable or GF/Flow requires a different binding mechanism.

need: Support multiple cheques within one registration dossier while keeping all cheque data canonical in Gravity Forms and editable by the Registration Officer in Gravity Flow.
candidates: Native Gravity Forms multi-column List field; Gravity Perks Nested Forms as fallback; custom repeater only after proven residual gap.
probe_or_evidence: Owner explicitly stated that one dossier may contain multiple cheques and asked for +/repeat behavior; fresh official Gravity Forms docs confirm List fields can add/remove rows and use multiple labeled columns.
observed_result: Gravity Forms List field natively provides add/remove row controls and multi-column rows. Gravity Flow docs allow selected form fields to be editable on Entry Details, but the exact List-field + scanner + save/reload behavior is not yet observed in target runtime.
decision: Record multi-cheque cardinality as a current requirement. Use native multi-column List field as first POC candidate; one row = one cheque. Do not select Nested Forms or build a custom repeater unless the native List-field POC demonstrates a concrete gap.
reopen_condition: Reopen candidate selection if List field cannot preserve multiple rows through the required Gravity Flow edit/save lifecycle, cannot support the scanner-to-active-row behavior, or its column model cannot satisfy required cheque validation/field semantics.

need: Select the canonical multi-cheque implementation surface and bind where PersianGravity Structured Scanner will run.
candidates: Gravity Flow Parent-Child Forms + generic PersianGravity Structured Scanner in Cheque Child Form; prior List Field and Nested Forms candidates no longer primary.
probe_or_evidence: Owner explicitly approved Parent-Child Forms for multi-cheque and instructed that scanner capability now be added to PersianGravity. Repository rules require generic Persian/Iranian Gravity Forms capability and prohibit SRWF-specific workflow/business logic/custom database.
observed_result: Parent-Child Forms is selected by Owner. Each cheque will be a separate Child Entry; scanner belongs in the Cheque Child Form and maps parsed profile outputs to ordinary GF fields. Runtime integration is still unexecuted.
decision: Use Gravity Flow Parent-Child Forms for the one-to-many cheque relationship. Implement PersianGravity Structured Scanner as a generic form capability: profile-based parse/validation + per-form output-to-GF-field mapping; no hard-coded SRWF IDs or Parent-Child persistence logic.
reopen_condition: Reopen only if bounded runtime POC shows the Child Form surface cannot reliably initialize the scanner, populate mapped fields, submit, or preserve the Parent relationship; a failed scanner implementation does not authorize a parallel database/workflow.

need: Close whether Structured Scanner owns persisted data or acts only as a controller that populates canonical Gravity Forms fields.
candidates: Persistent custom scanner field vs non-persistent controller element targeting ordinary GF fields.
probe_or_evidence: Owner explicitly asked to close the decision per the proposed design; Master/Playbook require Gravity Forms canonical data and minimal custom integration; PersianGravity repository rules prohibit SRWF-specific data/workflow ownership.
observed_result: The proposed controller model keeps cheque values in ordinary GF fields, permits manual correction, avoids raw QR persistence, and leaves Parent/Child relationship ownership to Gravity Flow.
decision: Structured Scanner v0.1 is a non-persistent controller element. It captures/parses input and populates mapped ordinary GF fields only; it does not own canonical cheque data and does not persist raw QR payload.
reopen_condition: Reopen only if the bounded Child Form POC proves that a non-persistent controller cannot reliably initialize/populate ordinary GF fields on the required surface.

need: Close the minimum deterministic Sayad v01 parser/output contract before implementation.
candidates: Seven-output conservative profile with atomic population vs stronger bank/version-specific validation rules.
probe_or_evidence: Owner explicitly asked to close the decision per the proposed conservative design. Current evidence contains one observed seven-segment real Sayad QR sample; cross-bank/version stability remains NOT_PROVEN.
observed_result: One real sample supports the seven semantic outputs but does not justify hard-coding additional assumptions such as fixed cheque-serial length or bank/branch formatting across issuers/versions.
decision: Sayad v01 POC contract is seven ordered outputs: qr_version, owner_type, owner_identifier, iban, bank_branch, cheque_serial, sayad_id. Parsing/population is atomic: if profile validation fails, no mapped target field is partially changed. Do not add stronger bank/version-specific validation until broader evidence supports it.
reopen_condition: Reopen if additional real-bank/version samples contradict the seven-output structure or the runtime POC requires a different binding/validation contract.

need: Move from closed scanner design into PersianGravity source-code implementation without further non-discriminating pre-work.
candidates: Implement now against latest stable supported official stack; defer only target-runtime validation until environment is available.
probe_or_evidence: Owner explicit instruction to remove unnecessary friction and begin coding; repository main inspected at PersianGravity 4.0.0. Fresh official evidence: WordPress 7.1, Gravity Forms 3.0, Gravity Flow 3.1, Parent-Child Forms 1.6.1 are current stable references.
observed_result: No implementation has yet been executed in this conversation. Stage 0 environment inventory remains open, so runtime compatibility is still NOT_PROVEN.
decision: Authorize focused source-code POC now. Use current documented APIs/latest stable patch levels at implementation time; keep scanner generic and non-persistent, Sayad v01 atomic, and Parent/Child relationship ownership outside PersianGravity.
reopen_condition: Reopen only if current official APIs or repository/runtime tests contradict the closed scanner contracts; runtime failure affects the surface, not the parent architecture.

need: Re-adjudicate the maintained extension used for repeatable cheque child Entries while preserving the already-closed generic scanner contract.
candidates: Gravity Perks Nested Forms; Gravity Flow Parent-Child Forms fallback; custom Parent Entry ID/link only as an isolated scanner harness, not selected production architecture.
probe_or_evidence: Owner explicitly changed the decision to Nested Forms and supplied decision rationale: both maintained options use modal/dynamic rendering; Nested Forms better aligns with in-form repeated-cheque UX and documented child-entry composition needs. Local product knowledge confirms GP Nested Forms is active, creates nested/repeatable child-entry relationships, and Gravity Flow 3.1.1 contains a compatibility fix for AJAX submissions inside editable Entry Details fields such as Nested Form.
observed_result: No runtime POC has yet been executed for Nested Forms in the target Gravity Flow surface. Scanner implementation has not started, so changing host does not require migration or code rollback.
decision: Select Gravity Perks Nested Forms as the current multi-cheque host. Keep PersianGravity Structured Scanner host-agnostic and inside the Cheque Child Form. Parent-Child Forms becomes fallback only if the bounded Nested Forms runtime POC fails. Do not adopt a custom Parent Entry ID/link relationship as production state.
reopen_condition: Reopen the host choice only if Nested Forms entitlement is unavailable on acceptable terms or the target POC fails child render/init, scanner population, submit/link persistence, or required finance composition. A candidate failure does not reopen the GF/Flow authority architecture.

need: Select the bounded first print-renderer candidate and Officer print UX without paid or parallel print dependencies.
candidates: Gravity PDF Free + SRWF-owned print layer; Browser Print as parallel production route; paid Gravity PDF templates/extensions; custom PDF engine.
probe_or_evidence: Owner-approved decision in the uploaded 2026-09-06 consultation; Master v1.6.4 D-17/§15/BP-10 currently deferred; no runtime print POC has been executed.
observed_result: Owner selected Gravity PDF Free as the first POC candidate, excluded paid templates/extensions, rejected a parallel Browser Print production route, and required a normal Officer path that does not depend on manual file download. Runtime fidelity remains NOT_PROVEN.
decision: D-17 remains POC_GATED / NOT_PROVEN. First-round candidate = Gravity PDF Free + SRWF-owned print layer. SRWF may own dossier template, field mapping, A4/page breaks, permissions, filename and print action, but not a PDF engine. A dedicated SRWF Print plugin is introduced only after a proven residual gap beyond template/configuration.
reopen_condition: Reopen on POC FAIL for Persian/RTL/ZWNJ, leading-zero National ID, Jalali date, amount/table, A4/page breaks, searchable/copyable logical Unicode, or inline-view/no-manual-download Officer UX; or on a material document requirement change. FAIL requires Owner re-adjudication of the next renderer and does not auto-authorize paid extensions or permanent Browser Print fallback.
